Hi all — attaching the artifacts we can provide immediately.

Summary of deliverables (attached):
1) no-train-attestation.pdf — short signed attestation confirming that for the scope of the Novus EU pilot (specified in the doc) Redwood will process prompts/responses for inference-only purposes and will not use them for model training, fine-tuning, or evaluation. This covers both hosted and dedicated modes for the duration of the pilot.
2) data-flow-eu.pdf — schematic showing compute in eu-west-1 region, KV-cache ephemeral scope, logs pushed to EU logging account with 30-day retention, and backups disabled for pilot workloads.
3) subprocessor-inventory.csv — list of subprocessors and which layer they touch (e.g., metrics, orchestration, storage).

Key clarifications (QA):
- Retention: inference request logs (request id + routing metadata) are retained for 30 days and are stored in EU-only buckets for the pilot. Full prompt/response payloads are not persisted beyond in-memory processing unless customer opt-in is set; when persisted, policy requires EU residency.
- Monitoring/alerts: aggregated telemetry (no raw payloads) may be routed to our global SRE channel; aggregated metrics do not contain PII or prompt content.
- Subprocessors: none of the listed subprocessors will export raw prompt/response content outside EU for model improvement. Transfers for third-party services (where applicable) are covered by SCCs and documented in the CSV.

I've run this by Rishi for the no-train language; he's added a short technical note about how we enforce no-training (sampling controls, disabled training pipelines, and audit hooks). Signing: I can provide an attestation signed by Redwood legal. Do you need a DocuSign flow or a PDF with an exec signature?

Attachments: no-train-attestation.pdf (PDF, 3 pages), data-flow-eu.pdf (PDF, 1 page), subprocessor-inventory.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
